title: Understanding the Position Function
text: The position function is given as $$r(t)=3.0t**{2}i-7.0t**{3}j-5.0t**{-2}k$$. $$To$$ $$find$$ $$the$$ $$speed$$, $$we$$ $$need$$ $$to$$ $$first$$ $$find$$ $$the$$ $$velocity$$ $$by$$ $$differentiating$$ $$the$$ $$position$$ $$function$$ $$with$$ $$respect$$ $$to$$ $$time$$.

title: Differentiating the Position Function
text: Differentiate each component of the position function with respect to time $$t$$. Remember that the derivative of $$t**{n}$$ is n*$$t**{n-1}$$.

title: Calculate the Velocity Components
text:
Differentiate each component:
- For the i component: 3.0*$$t**{2}$$ becomes $$6t$$
- For the j component: -7.0*$$t**{3}$$ becomes -21.0*$$t**{2}$$
- For the k component: -5.0*$$t**{-2}$$ becomes 10.0*$$t**{-3}$$

title: Finding the Speed
text: The speed is the magnitude of the velocity vector. Use the formula: speed $$=$$ sqrt(($$v_{x}$$)**2+($$v_{y}$$)**2+($$v_{z}$$)**2).

title: Calculate the Speed at $$t=1.0\, \text{s}$$
text:
Substitute $$t=1.0$$ into the velocity components and calculate the magnitude:
- $$v_{x}=6.0\cdot1.0-v_{y}$$ $$=$$ -21.0*$$1.0**{2}$$
- $$v_{z}=10.0\cdot1.0**{-3}$$
